topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the structure, background, and specific learning outcomes for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Cellular origins, tissue architecture, and experimental modeling of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer arises from genetic alterations and failures of cellular differentiation within structured tissues, alongside experimental methods for modeling tumor cells in vitro.

topics.label: Pathology and progression of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the histological hallmarks, anatomical routes, and diagnostic significance of local tissue invasion, metastatic spread, and the stepwise transition from benign precursors to malignant tumors.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and mechanisms of clinical disease and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the conventions for classifying and naming tumors while detailing the pathophysiological mechanisms through which both benign and malignant growths cause illness and death.

topics.label: Epidemiology and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse cancer incidence patterns in humans and compare tumor occurrence across diverse animal species and multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the early clinical signs of cancer and assess the utility, techniques, and histological basis of screening programmes across different organ systems.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reiterating the learning outcomes and looking ahead to the associated practical sessions.
